a2-ls-s01-cp1-001: The x-intercept is where the line crosses the x-axis, so y = 0 there: 3x - 4(0) = 12, so 3x = 12 and x = 4.
The y-intercept is where the line crosses the y-axis, so x = 0 there: 3(0) - 4y = 12, so -4y = 12 and y = -3.
Write each intercept as a point: x-intercept (4, 0), y-intercept (0, -3).
a2-ls-s01-cp1-002: Set y = 0 for the x-intercept: 5x + 2(0) = -20, so 5x = -20 and x = -4.
Set x = 0 for the y-intercept: 5(0) + 2y = -20, so 2y = -20 and y = -10.
Write each intercept as a point: x-intercept (-4, 0), y-intercept (0, -10).
a2-ls-s01-cp1-003: Set y = 0 for the x-intercept: -2x + 6(0) = 18, so -2x = 18 and x = -9.
Set x = 0 for the y-intercept: -2(0) + 6y = 18, so 6y = 18 and y = 3.
Write each intercept as a point: x-intercept (-9, 0), y-intercept (0, 3).
a2-ls-s02-cp2-001: Use m = (y₂ - y₁)/(x₂ - x₁) with (x₁, y₁) = (1, 2) and (x₂, y₂) = (5, 10).
Change in y: 10 - 2 = 8. Change in x: 5 - 1 = 4.
a2-ls-s02-cp2-002: Use m = (y₂ - y₁)/(x₂ - x₁) with (x₁, y₁) = (-3, 4) and (x₂, y₂) = (1, -4).
Change in y: -4 - 4 = -8. Change in x: 1 - (-3) = 4.
a2-ls-s02-cp2-004: Use m = (y₂ - y₁)/(x₂ - x₁) with (0, 3) and (7, 3).
Change in y: 3 - 3 = 0. Change in x: 7 - 0 = 7.
m = 0/7 = 0, so the line is horizontal.
a2-ls-s02-cp2-005: Use m = (y₂ - y₁)/(x₂ - x₁) with (-5, -2) and (5, 2).
Change in y: 2 - (-2) = 4. Change in x: 5 - (-5) = 10.
a2-ls-s02-cp1-001: Evaluate the endpoints: f(1) = 1² = 1 and f(4) = 4² = 16.
a2-ls-s02-cp1-002: Evaluate the endpoints: f(-1) = (-1)² - 3(-1) = 1 + 3 = 4 and f(2) = 2² - 3(2) = 4 - 6 = -2.
a2-ls-s02-cp1-003: Evaluate the endpoints: f(0) = 2⁰ = 1 and f(3) = 2³ = 8.
a2-ls-s02-cp1-004: Evaluate the endpoints: f(-2) = (-2)³ = -8 and f(1) = 1³ = 1.
a2-ls-s02-honors-003: Average rate of change on [a, a + h] = (f(a + h) - f(a))/((a + h) - a) = ((a + h)² - a²)/h.
Expand: (a + h)² - a² = a² + 2ah + h² - a² = 2ah + h².
a2-ls-s03-cp2-004: The $50 sign-up fee is paid once, so it is the starting value (the intercept).
The $25 is added every month, so it is the rate of change (the slope) per month m.
a2-ls-s03-cp1-004: In h = -0.6t + 48, the constant 48 is the value of h when t = 0.
t = 0 is the moment the candle is lit, before any time has passed.
So 48 cm is the candle's initial height.
a2-ls-s03-cp1-005: The candle burns out when its height is 0, so set h = 0: -0.6t + 48 = 0.
Divide by 0.6: t = 48/0.6 = 80, so it burns out after 80 hours.
a2-ls-s03-honors-002: Treat the two facts as points (C, K): (0, 273.15) and (100, 373.15).
At C = 0, K = 273.15, so the intercept is 273.15 and K = C + 273.15, with slope 1.
a2-ls-s04-cp1-001: The variable drops out and the statement is always true, so the equations describe the same line: infinitely many solutions.
a2-ls-s04-cp1-002: The statement is false for every x, so the lines are parallel: no solution.
a2-ls-s04-cp1-003: The statement is always true, so the two equations are the same line: infinitely many solutions.
a2-ls-s05-cp1-005: When both variables cancel, what is left is a statement about numbers only.
0 = 0 is true no matter what x and y are.
So every point on one line is also on the other: the equations describe the same line and there are infinitely many solutions.
a2-ls-s05-cp1-009: Downstream the current helps: speed = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 km/h, so b + c = 18.
Upstream the current slows the boat: speed = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 km/h, so b - c = 12.
Add the equations: 2b = 30, so b = 15. Then c = 18 - 15 = 3.
The boat goes 15 km/h in still water and the current is 3 km/h.
a2-ls-s06-cp1-006: To isolate y in -2y > 6x - 4, divide every term by -2.
Dividing (or multiplying) an inequality by a negative number reverses the inequality sign.
a2-ls-s07-cp2-005: For a linear objective, the lines where it has a fixed value are parallel; increasing the value slides the line across the region.
The last point of the region the line touches as it slides is a corner of the region.
So the maximum (and the minimum) of a bounded region occurs at a vertex.
a2-ls-s07-cp2-006: Each muffin uses 1 cup and each cake uses 3 cups, so x muffins and y cakes use 1·x + 3·y cups.
The flour used cannot be more than the 30 cups available.
a2-ls-s02-cp1-012: The slope of y = -4x + 1 is -4, so a perpendicular line has slope -1/(-4) = 1/4 (the negative reciprocal).
The lines with slope 1/4 are y = (1/4)x, x - 4y = 8 and y = 0.25x - 3.
a2-ls-s02-cp1-016: Slope is change in y over change in x: m = (1 - 5)/(6 - 2) = -4/4 = -1.
The student divided change in x by change in y: (6 - 2)/(1 - 5) = 4/(-4) = -1.
Both happen to equal -1 only because |Δy| = |Δx| here; the method is upside down and would give the wrong slope for other points.
a2-ls-s02-cp2-011: y = 7 has the same y-value, 7, for every x, so its graph is a horizontal line.
Between any two points the change in y is 0.
a2-ls-s02-cp1-017: Set it equal to 2: (10 - k)/3 = 2, so 10 - k = 6.
a2-ls-s03-cp1-017: In C = 25m + 50 the intercept 50 is the one-time sign-up fee and the slope 25 is the monthly rate, so C is linear, not exponential.
True: the sign-up fee is $50, the monthly rate is $25, C(12) = 350 and after 6 months the cost is $200.
a2-ls-s03-cp1-018: A linear model adds the same amount in each equal time step (constant difference).
A population that doubles every hour multiplies by 2 each hour (constant ratio), so its increases keep growing.
That is exponential growth, so the bacteria population is not well modeled by a linear function.
a2-ls-s03-cp2-005: The cost goes up by $11 for every month, so the rate is 11 dollars per month.
There is no starting fee, so the cost is 0 when m = 0.
a2-ls-s03-honors-005: Plan A costs 40 + 0.10m and plan B costs 0.25m for m minutes.
m = 40/0.15 ≈ 266.67, so the plans cost the same at about 266.7 minutes (about 267).
a2-ls-s04-cp1-016: x = 2 is only half of the answer: a solution of a system in two variables is an ordered pair (x, y).
Check in 2x + y = 8: 2(2) + 4 = 8. The solution is (2, 4).
a2-ls-s04-honors-005: A linear system has no solution when the lines are parallel: same slope, different y-intercepts.
The slopes are k and 3, so the lines are parallel when k = 3.
The intercepts are 2 and -5, which are different, so k = 3 gives no solution.
a2-ls-s04-cp2-009: The point satisfies both equations, so yes, it is a solution.
a2-ls-s05-cp1-017: (a) Count: a + c = 300 tickets. Value: 9a + 6c = 2250 dollars.
(b) Multiply the count equation by 6: 6a + 6c = 1800. Subtract it from 9a + 6c = 2250: 3a = 450.
a2-ls-s05-cp1-018: When both variables cancel, the result is a statement about numbers only.
0 = 5 is false no matter what x and y are.
So no point satisfies both equations: the lines are parallel and the system has no solution.
a2-ls-s05-cp1-019: When both variables cancel, the result is a statement about numbers only.
0 = 0 is true no matter what x and y are.
So the two equations are equivalent (the same line), and the system has infinitely many solutions.
a2-ls-s05-honors-008: Downstream: 36 ÷ 2 = 18 mph, so b + c = 18. Upstream: 36 ÷ 3 = 12 mph, so b - c = 12.
The boat's speed is 15 mph and the current is 3 mph.
a2-ls-s06-cp1-008: Substitute each point into y ≤ -x + 4 and check whether the left side is at most the right side.
(0, 0): 0 ≤ 4 true. (2, 2): 2 ≤ 2 true (on the boundary, allowed by ≤). (5, -1): -1 ≤ -1 true.
a2-ls-s06-cp1-009: Substitute each point into 2x - 3y > 6; boundary points (where 2x - 3y = 6) do not count because > is strict.
a2-ls-s06-cp1-011: A point is a solution only if it satisfies x + y < 5, x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 1.
(-1, 2) fails x ≥ 0. (3, 0) fails y ≥ 1. (4, 1) fails x + y < 5 because 5 < 5 is false.
a2-ls-s06-cp1-012: The boundary line has y-intercept -1 and rises 2 for every 1 to the right, so it is y = 2x - 1.
The boundary is dashed, so points on the line are not included: the symbol is strict (< or >).
The region above the line is shaded, so y > 2x - 1.
a2-ls-s06-cp1-013: The boundary has y-intercept 3 and falls 1 for every 2 to the right, so it is y = -(1/2)x + 3.
The boundary is solid, so points on the line are included: ≤ or ≥.
The region below the line is shaded, so y ≤ -(1/2)x + 3.
a2-ls-s06-honors-005: (a) Earnings are $15 per tutoring hour and $12 per retail hour, and must be at least $270: 15x + 12y ≥ 270.
(d) With y = 0: 15x ≥ 270, so x ≥ 18; the minimum is 18 hours (and 18 ≤ 20).
a2-ls-s06-cp1-015: Divide both sides by -3. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality: x < -2.
The student kept the > sign; the correct solution is x < -2.
a2-ls-s06-cp2-008: Substitute x = 2 and y = 1 into y < x.
a2-ls-s06-cp1-016: The line through (0, -2) with slope 3 is y = 3x - 2.
A solid line means points on the line are included, so use ≥ or ≤.
The region above the line has larger y-values: y ≥ 3x - 2.
a2-ls-s07-cp1-008: The maximum of a linear objective over a bounded region occurs at a vertex, so evaluate P = 5x + 2y at each vertex.
a2-ls-s07-cp1-009: Evaluate P = x + 4y at each vertex of the region.
a2-ls-s07-cp1-010: The minimum of a linear objective over the region occurs at a vertex, so evaluate C = 3x + y at each one.
a2-ls-s07-cp1-011: The constraints are 2x + y ≤ 16 (hours) and x + y ≤ 10 (items), with x, y ≥ 0.
a2-ls-s07-cp1-012: The constraints are the inequalities that limit the possible choices (time, materials, budget, nonnegativity).
The set of points that satisfies every constraint at once is the feasible region.
So the constraints describe the feasible region.
a2-ls-s07-cp1-013: Let x = hours on machine A and y = hours on machine B; the units constraint is 5x + 3y ≥ 30, with x ≤ 6 and y ≤ 6.
Also 6 ≤ 6 and 0 ≤ 6 are true, so yes, (6, 0) is feasible: it produces exactly 5(6) = 30 units.
a2-ls-s07-honors-006: With x, y ≥ 0 the region extends without end to the right and upward, so x or y can be as large as we like.
P = x + y keeps increasing in that direction, so it has no largest value: no maximum.
P cannot decrease forever, though: its least value on the region occurs at a vertex, so a minimum can exist.
a2-ls-s03-cp1-019: In h = 30 - 2.5t the slope is -2.5 cm/h (it loses 2.5 cm each hour) and the intercept is 30 cm, not 2.5.
Burns out when h = 0: 30 - 2.5t = 0, so t = 30/2.5 = 12 hours.
True: it burns out after 12 hours, after 4 hours it is 20 cm tall, and the slope is -2.5 cm/h.
a2-ls-s06-honors-006: y > x + 2 and y < x - 1 have parallel boundaries (both slope 1); one asks for points above the higher line, the other for points below the lower line, so no point does both.
x ≥ 4 and x < 2 contradict each other: no number is both at least 4 and less than 2.
The other systems have points in common: (0, 0) satisfies y < 3 and y > -3; (1, 1) satisfies y ≥ 0 and x ≥ 0; (-2, 0) satisfies y > x and y < -x.
The empty systems are y > x + 2 and y < x - 1, and x ≥ 4 and x < 2.
a2-ls-s07-cp1-014: The maximum of P = 2x + 3y occurs at a vertex, so evaluate it at each one.
a2-ls-s07-cp1-015: The minimum of C = 4x + 3y occurs at a vertex, so evaluate it at each one.
a2-ls-s07-cp1-016: The maximum of P = 6x + y occurs at a vertex, so evaluate it at each one.
a2-ls-s01-honors-009: Solve for y: add x to both sides, -7y = x - 8.
The coefficient of x is the slope: -1/7.
a2-ls-s01-honors-012: Solve for y: subtract 3x from both sides, y = -3x + 3.
The equation is now in slope-intercept form y = mx + b.
The slope is the coefficient of x: -3.
a2-ls-s06-cp2-009: Substitute x = -1 and y = -1 into y ≥ -x + 1.
Right side: -(-1) + 1 = 1 + 1 = 2, so the inequality reads -1 ≥ 2.
-1 ≥ 2 is false, so (-1, -1) is not a solution: No.
a2-ls-s06-cp2-013: Substitute x = 2 and y = 0 into y ≤ 2x - 1.
Right side: 2(2) - 1 = 3, so the inequality reads 0 ≤ 3.
0 ≤ 3 is true, so (2, 0) is a solution: Yes.
a2-ls-s06-honors-007: Substitute x = 3 and y = 4 into y ≥ x + 1.
Right side: 3 + 1 = 4, so the inequality reads 4 ≥ 4.
4 ≥ 4 is true (the point is on the solid boundary), so (3, 4) is a solution: Yes.
a2-ls-s06-honors-011: Substitute x = 0 and y = 0 into y ≤ -2x + 3.
Right side: -2(0) + 3 = 3, so the inequality reads 0 ≤ 3.
0 ≤ 3 is true, so (0, 0) is a solution: Yes.
a2-ls-s05-cp1-pc02: The y-terms have opposite coefficients, so add the equations: (x + y) + (x - y) = 3 + 5, giving 2x = 8.
Substitute into x + y = 3: 4 + y = 3, so y = -1.
a2-ls-s02-cp1-pc01: Use m = (y₂ - y₁)/(x₂ - x₁) with (-1, -3) and (2, 12).
Change in y: 12 - (-3) = 15. Change in x: 2 - (-1) = 3.
